findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it an internet-routable endpoint. Combined with an 'admin' master user and a password sourced from a variable, this exposes the database to credential attacks from outside the VPC.
storage_encrypted = false disables RDS storage encryption, leaving database files, automated snapshots and underlying volumes holding customer data (employee names and addresses) in cleartext.

The master password is passed as var.password and the same value is interpolated into EC2 user data. It is persisted in cleartext in Terraform state and plan output instead of being managed via Secrets Manager or RDS-managed master passwords.

The database master username and password are written into the EC2 user_data script, which is retrievable in cleartext from the instance metadata service (http://169.254.169.254/latest/user-data) and from the EC2 DescribeInstanceAttribute API by any principal with ec2:* (which this instance's own role has).

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains available. With DB credentials in user data and a wildcard instance profile attached, a server-side request forgery in the PHP application would yield both the role credentials and the database password.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the volume holding the plaintext credential include file (/var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc) and cached data is likely unencrypted at rest.

The instance serves an HTTP-only PHP form collecting personal data (name, address) with no TLS termination, and its public DNS is exported, indicating internet reachability; submitted data traverses the network in cleartext.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". Attached to the role of an internet-facing EC2 instance, a compromise yields near-total control of S3 data, EC2 (including privilege escalation by launching instances with other roles) and RDS (including snapshot exfiltration and master password reset).
The database security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unconstrained outbound path usable for data exfiltration or command-and-control after a compromise.
MySQL port 3306 is opened to the whole VPC CIDR rather than being scoped to the application instance's security group, so any workload in the VPC can reach the database directly.
The master user is set to the predictable default 'admin', which removes any obscurity from brute-force and credential-stuffing attempts against a publicly accessible endpoint.

The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the database accepts unencrypted client connections; the generated PHP client also calls mysqli_connect without SSL options, meaning credentials and query data cross the network in cleartext.
